c.v: Should a 20 year old roof be replaced?

runs.v: It depends on what the roof is made of. A 3-tab asphalt roof reaches the end of its rated life at about 20 years and architectural asphalt at about 30, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, so a 20-year-old 3-tab roof with curling tabs, granule loss, soft decking, or a leak in more than one spot is usually due for a full replacement, while a 20-year-old slate or standing-seam metal roof is mid-life and needs flashing work instead. Roof repairs in Bloomfield can extend the roof's lifespan significantly when the deck is sound, and free roof inspections are available to assess repair needs in Bloomfield: a professional inspection of the home's roof settles the question, and Newark Quality Roofing provides it at no charge, with photographs of what it finds.

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: Roofers use a rule of thumb that once damage covers more than about 25% of a roof, replacement usually costs less over time than continued repairs, and New Jersey's code draws a similar line: on commercial, multi-family, and attached buildings, work on more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months needs a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. A building permit is required for full roof replacements on those New Jersey buildings, while a detached one- or two-family re-roof counts as ordinary maintenance with no permit. Roof replacements often require a full tear-off of old materials, and in Bloomfield the permit line applies to garden apartments, condominiums, and corridor commercial buildings, not to a detached one- or two-family home.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a roof replacement in Bloomfield, NJ?

runs.v: A complete tear-off and re-roof of the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family home in Bloomfield counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and requires no construction permit, inspection, or notice to the construction official, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. A commercial, multi-family, or attached building requires a permit from the Township of Bloomfield's construction office once the work exceeds 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period, and any structural change to rafters or trusses triggers a permit, so Bloomfield's garden apartments, condominiums, and three-family and larger buildings follow the permit path while a detached two-family home stays exempt.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace a Bloomfield roof?

runs.v: Replace a roof when damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost; repair a roof when the damage stays localized on an asphalt roof under 10–15 years old. The 25–30% area rule and the 50% cost rule are contractor-consensus thresholds, per Modernize and published NJ contractor pricing, and a localized repair can cost 5 to 10 times less than replacement, per Home Depot and published NJ contractor pricing. A covering at or past its InterNACHI-rated service life favors full replacement.

faqs.q: Does a full tear-off remove the existing roof, or can a new roof go over it?

runs.v: Usually the old roof comes off. The NJ Rehabilitation Subcode (N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4) requires removal to the bare deck when the roof is water-soaked, is wood shake, slate, clay, cement, or asbestos-cement tile, or already carries 2 or more layers, and a full tear-off lets deteriorated sheathing on the pre-war stock be replaced, while a recover over one sound layer hides the deck and adds weight to framing designed for one layer.
